text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik said the government and the National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) were in discussions on whether the central bank should not follow its Czech counterpart and ease its monetary policy.

- NBS Governor Vladimir Masar said the bank was not planning to soften its policy but added that it might do so if foreign trade shows positive development, or if funds accumulated by import deposits drain liquidity from the market and are held by the NBS.

- Nomura International Plc said it did not want to buy the Slovak stake in the largest Czech commercial bank Komercni Banka. Nomura said it was not in discussions with the Slovak government over privatisation of state banks but added that it would be interested in a bank sell-off.
- Slovakia's second largest commercial bank IRB said it had completed changing its stock from bearer shares to registered and publicly traded stocks.

- Slovenske Elektrarne (SE), the state-owned energy monopoly, said it wanted to achieve a sovereign rating to issue unspecified tranche of Eurobonds. SE said its investment plans will require 47.45 billion crowns by the year 2010.

- Ladislav Pittner, a parliamentary deputy of the oposition Christian Democratic Movement (KDH) demands that the police to re-open investigations of the murder of former policeman Robert Remias linked to the kidnapping of the president's son.

- U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright on Thursday told Foreign Minister Pavol Hamzik that Bratislava should adopt a law on minority languages and that the ruling coalition should allow the opposition to participate in the control of the secret service and privatisation.
SME - President Michal Kovac said he was considering taking the government to the Constitutional Court for attempts to postpone a referendum on direct presidential elections.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin is expected to sign several treaties with Slovakia during his visit to Bratislava next week, including agreements on liberalistion of mututal trade and border cooperation.
- Oil refiner Slovnaft plans to process some 5.11 million tonnes of crude oil in 1997 on turnover of 44.3 billion crowns.

- The overall length of Slovakia's motorways will increase to 660 kilometres by the year 2005 from the current 215 kilometres. This year's 14 billion crowns for motorway construction should soon return some 10 billion crowns back to the state coffers through taxes from firms participating in the project and through saved unemployment benefits.
- The Finance Ministry said it planned easing its tax policy to support the flow of investment into the economy.
PRAVDA - Import deposits, implemented by the government to fight foreign trade problems, should total some 11 billion crowns.
- Steel producer VSZ said it plans to participate in building a Toyota plant for car production in Slovakia.
